status.en: 123 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 123 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen repeatedly assaulted former Super Eagles captain Segun Odegbami at his home in Abeokuta, wounding him but he survived the machete attack. Security personnel continued to be targeted, with a university guard killed while returning home with his wife and another guard shot dead in Plateau, while gunmen also attacked a mining site in Plateau, leaving three feared dead, and shot a herder dead in the same state. Police launched a manhunt for the assailants of Odegbami and vowed to apprehend the perpetrators. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn angrep gjentatte ganger den tidligere Super Eagles-kapteinen Segun Odegbami i hans hjem i Abeokuta, såret ham, men han overlevde machetteangrepet. Sikkerhetspersonell fortsatte å bli målrettet, med en universitetsvakt drept mens han var på vei hjem med sin kone og en annen vakt skutt død i Plateau, mens væpnede menn også angrep en gruveplass i Plateau, hvor tre fryktes døde, og skjøt en hyrde død i samme delstat. Politiet igangsatte en etterforskning av Odegbamis angripere og lovet å pågripe gjerningspersonene. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
